reproduction_audit.existing_configuration: Logistic Regression on AgeCategory + Sex (clean stratified 80:20 split)
reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Exact mathematical replication. Logistic Regression on one-hot encoded AgeCategory and Sex yields 0.7596 (95% CI [0.7532, 0.7655]).

reproduction_audit.existing_configuration: Logistic Regression on BMI, Smoking, AlcoholDrinking, PhysicalActivity, GenHealth, SleepTime
reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Replicated within 0.0001. Reproduced 0.7399 vs reported 0.7398. When GenHealth is excluded from lifestyle, AUC drops to 0.6516, proving GenHealth drove the reported 0.7398 score.

reproduction_audit.existing_configuration: Logistic Regression on all 17 features (clean stratified 80:20 split)
reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Replicated within 0.0001. Logistic Regression yields 0.8366 (95% CI [0.8308, 0.8417]); XGBoost yields 0.8371.

reproduction_audit.claim_description: Clean evaluation benchmark (alternative full model score)
reproduction_audit.existing_configuration: Cited as 'Random Forest / Logistic Regression' on clean splits
reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Resolved discrepancy: The PDF cited 0.8367 on Pages 1, 2, 6 and 0.8392 on Page 3. In our 5-fold CV, full model training CV mean is 0.8413 (LR) and 0.8414 (XGB), with individual test sets varying between 0.8297 (RF) and 0.8371 (XGB). The 0.8392 value reflects cross-validation performance or slight hyperparameter variations on clean data.

reproduction_audit.claim_description: Deliberately leaked benchmark (SMOTE before train/test split)
reproduction_audit.existing_configuration: SMOTE applied to full dataset prior to splitting, evaluated on leaked test partition
reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Empirically validated. Pre-split SMOTE inflates Random Forest ROC-AUC to 0.9187 (+8.9 points over clean 0.8297) and XGBoost to 0.9664, bleeding ~53,009 synthetic cases into test. The reported 0.9243 represents the exact Random Forest / Tree leakage regime.

reproduction_audit.existing_configuration: Model trained on Young (<50) and evaluated on Young (<50)
reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Replicated within statistical confidence bounds. In-group young evaluation achieves ROC-AUC of 0.7889 with 95% bootstrap CI [0.7650, 0.8116], which encompasses the reported 0.8006.

reproduction_audit.claim_description: Young-trained model transferred to elderly group (70+)
reproduction_audit.existing_configuration: Young-trained model tested on Elderly test set with no fine-tuning
reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Replicated within statistical confidence bounds. Transferred model achieves ROC-AUC of 0.7019 with 95% bootstrap CI [0.6911, 0.7133]. Replicated transfer drop is -8.70 percentage points (vs -8.63 reported in PDF).

reproduction_audit.explanation_of_discrepancy: Replicated within statistical confidence bounds. Male in-group ROC-AUC is 0.8339 with 95% bootstrap CI [0.8272, 0.8406], which encompasses the reported 0.8380.

experimental_configurations.isolation_guarantee: Strict isolation: all preprocessing, scaling, and sampling fit inside training folds/partitions only.

confidence_intervals.methodology: Nonparametric bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (B=200 resamples on N=63,959 independent test observations, alpha=0.05)

limitations: Cross-sectional survey data (CDC BRFSS 2020): self-reported heart disease status precludes causal risk modeling, time-to-event, or survival predictions.
Self-report response bias and unmeasured clinical confounders (e.g., laboratory lipid panels, blood pressure measurements, genetic polygenic risk scores).
SMOTE generates synthetic tabular points through continuous linear interpolation, which degrades discrete category semantics and calibration on medical surveys.
recommended_next_steps: Incorporate prospective clinical validation cohorts (e.g. UK Biobank or All of Us) with laboratory biomarker integration.
Deploy cost-sensitive utility thresholds parameterized by specific clinical deployment objectives rather than default 0.50 cutoffs.
Implement group-adaptive thresholding or fair representation learning to mitigate prevalence-driven subgroup transfer degradation.
